audit_findings.title: Affiliate cash flows appear double-counted in OE and the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed affiliate distributions were $116.0 million in 2025, $138.7 million in 2024 and $155.1 million in 2023; the bridge separately adds $684.6 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Affiliate distributions enter consolidated operating cash flow and therefore OE, while the affiliates' investment carrying value is also added through the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: The Company received distributions from Rivers Des Plaines of $ 68.5 million in 2025, $ 92.2 million in 2024 and $ 111.1 million in 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not yet a demonstrated error, because the OE reconciliation showing whether distributions were purged was not supplied. It is material: 2025 distributions equal 33.4% of the $347.2 million anchor, and the separately added stake equals 11.9% of base equity value. Retaining both could substantially overstate every scenario.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to the cash-flow statement and remove all Rivers Des Plaines and MVG distributions and other affiliate cash flows before rerunning the trend anchor and scenarios, unless the separate stake value is removed instead.

audit_findings.title: Puttable noncontrolling interests create a claim mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: $50 million redeemable noncontrolling interest at June 30, 2026, equivalent to $0.71 per diluted share; ownership-share OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated OE includes cash flows from United Tote and Casino Salem, while CHDN common shares are the denominator and no redeemable NCI claim is deducted in the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: The redeemable noncontrolling interest is initially accounted for at fair value and subsequently adjusted to the greater of the redemption value or the carrying value.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted $50 million claim is demonstrated, but its direct bridge effect alone would reduce base value from $81.75 to approximately $81.04 per share and would not change the current price comparison. Materiality remains unresolved because the record does not allocate recurring OE, capex, redemption-value growth or settlement obligations between CHDN and the minority holders.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the put agreements and subsidiary-level cash-flow statements; either calculate CHDN's ownership share of OE and capex or deduct the contractual redemption value and model future accretion, then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The stake bridge appears to omit its associated deferred-tax claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $103.2 million directly associated deferred-tax liability, equal to $1.47 per diluted share and 1.8% of $5,759 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds the affiliate investment carrying value that was increased when the deferred-tax liability was recorded, without deducting the matching tax claim
audit_findings.evidence: We also recognized a $ 103.2 million deferred tax liability and a corresponding increase in our investment in unconsolidated affiliates related to an entity we acquired in conjunction with our acquisition of the Clairvest ownership stake in Midwest Gaming.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied $684.6 million bridge amount matches the filed investment carrying value, so the mismatch is demonstrated unless an undocumented after-tax adjustment exists. Deducting the filed $103.2 million would reduce base value from $81.75 to about $80.28 per share and the buy-below level from $57.22 to about $56.19. It would not change the conclusion that the market price exceeds bear and base values but remains below bull value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the bridge to the latest tax-basis schedule and replace the gross carrying value with an independently supported after-tax stake value; rerun the bridge if the associated liability differs from $103.2 million.

audit_findings.title: Committed development spending is not visible in the smooth OE forecast
audit_findings.magnitude: $460-$500 million of announced project spending for the first-turn building and Rockingham, equal to $6.53-$7.10 per diluted share before discounting and 9.4%-10.3% of base operating PV
audit_findings.mechanism: Committed project capital should reduce forecast OE in the construction years; a smooth growth forecast with a null perimeter may capture later earnings without the preceding cash outlays
audit_findings.evidence: The Company is also investing $280-$300 million to build a new building on the first turn of the Churchill Downs Racetrack between the First Turn Club and the Skye Terrace.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitments are filed and the valuation contains no explicit project-capital schedule, making the omission reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion. The gross commitments are comparable to almost the entire $7.14 per-share gap between market price and bull value, although the exact valuation effect depends on spending timing, amounts already incurred and the growth benefits included.
audit_findings.action: Build a 2026-2028 project-capital schedule for the first-turn building and Rockingham, reconcile it to 2026 spending already incurred and forecast OE, prevent project earnings from entering before opening, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Historical interest expense may not represent refinancing economics
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.3 billion of notes mature in 2027-2028; each 1 percentage-point change in refinancing cost would change pretax annual interest by approximately $13 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE model, refinancing coupons, fees and variable-rate exposure flow directly through interest expense and recurring OE
audit_findings.evidence: Access to capital markets and the terms under which we would fund the obligations are subject to our ability to access the market and other market conditions.
audit_findings.explanation: No valuation error is presently demonstrated. The latest filing still shows $600 million of 5.50% notes due in 2027 and $700 million of 4.75% notes due in 2028, with future refinancing terms unknown. This is a forward-looking exposure that should be monitored until actual terms or a supportable refinancing assumption exist.
audit_findings.action: Monitor refinancing filings and debt-market transactions; once terms are known, update annual interest expense for coupons, issuance fees and funding mix and rerun OE and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A one-time insurance recovery remains a possible OE contaminant
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.5 million, equal to 1.0% of the $347.2 million anchor; even a full direct anchor adjustment would reduce base value by approximately $0.70 per share, with the actual trend effect smaller
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring insurance recovery can enter operating cash flow and OE and slightly raise the fitted historical trend anchor
audit_findings.evidence: The Virginia HRM increase was primarily due to a $24.1 million net increase from our Northern Virginia venues, which includes $3.5 million of one-time business interruption insurance recovery related to the delayed opening of The Rose Gaming Resort in fourth quarter 2024, and a $1.8 million decrease in government relations expense, partially offset by a $7.2 million net decrease primarily from our Western and Southern Virginia venues.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion is unresolved because the OE reconciliation was not supplied. Even if the entire recovery were embedded directly in the anchor, the computed effect is about $49 million of operating value or $0.70 per share, insufficient to change the scenario or price conclusion; fitting the lower multi-year trend should further reduce the effect.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the $3.5 million recovery was removed from 2025 OE; if included, remove it, refit the log-trend anchor and document the resulting immaterial change.
